## What it is

We combined from [Oregon Department of Forestry (2000-2022)](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/mattop/fire-occurrence-and-cause-data-2000-2022) and the [US Wildfire Dataset (2014-2025)](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/firecastrl/us-wildfire-dataset/data) to explore how environmental and human related factors differently predict human-caused versus lightning-caused wildfires in Oregon. Each author was responsible for coding a model (e.g., Gradient Boosting, kNN, Random Forest, Decision Tree), and together we combine all models into a single Ensemble model. The code files are available as Jupyter Notebooks and can be used to replicate our findings easily with Google Drive. See the links section below.

## What I did

- Applied a spatio-temporal join using Geopandas to merge the ODF and US Wildfire data.
- Coded and analyzed data using the kNN model.
- Wrote the background, data, method, ensemble, results, and limitations sections.
- Model results were in line with prior studies, suggesting good model fit for Oregon, specifically.
- Model results for lightning vs. human features achieved 85% accuracy.
- The Ensemble model predicted a large (173k acre), naturally caused fire (lightning), but not a large (50k acre) human caused.
- The Ensemble model predicted whether the same fires were lightning vs. human caused.
